text:
Can you help me write the project summary for a grant application? I'm the managing attorney at a two-lawyer legal aid clinic that represents tenants facing eviction. We're applying to our state bar foundation for $90,000 to hire a third attorney for two years.

Facts:
- Last year 1,140 eviction cases were filed in our county. We represented the tenant in 163 of them.
- In the cases where we represented the tenant, 58% ended with the tenant staying in the home or getting at least 60 days to move. We don't have a comparable number for tenants without a lawyer.
- We turned away about 300 tenants last year because no attorney was free.
- Our two attorneys each carry about 80 open cases. One of them is leaving in June.
- A third attorney would cost $78,000 a year with benefits. The foundation's maximum award is $45,000 a year.
- The county gives us $60,000 a year, and that contract is up for renewal in October.

The project summary has to be 300 words or less.

Before I draft, I need a few answers. Each one changes what the summary can honestly say.

1. **Where does the rest of the salary come from?** The attorney costs $78,000 a year and the foundation pays at most $45,000, so there's a $33,000 gap each year. Reviewers will look for it. Will county money, another grant or your general budget cover it, and is that money committed or still pending?

2. **Is this a new position or a replacement?** If the third attorney mainly fills the seat of the one leaving in June, the grant keeps you at two lawyers rather than growing to three. That calls for a different argument: protecting your capacity instead of expanding it. Which June do you mean, and do you have funding to replace the departing attorney separately?

3. **Where does the county contract stand?** Today is November 16, 2026, so "up for renewal in October" could mean last month or October 2027. Was it renewed, and is any of that $60,000 part of the plan for this position?

4. **What does the foundation want to see?** Do they publish funding priorities, scoring criteria or required parts for the summary (for example need, activities, outcomes, sustainability)? If you can paste them, I'll match their wording and order.

5. **What will a third attorney achieve, and what happens after two years?** For example, how many more tenants a year you expect to represent (my rough math from your caseloads is about 80 open cases at a time), and any plan to keep the position funded after the grant ends. Please also give me your clinic's name and county if you'd like them in the draft.

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write around them without guessing.

1. A family fund has pledged $20,000 a year for two years toward the new attorney. The rest of the gap comes from our general budget.

2. June 2027. She's agreed to spend her last month training the new hire. I don't know if we have separate funding to replace her.

3. It's up in October 2027. I can't promise the county will renew it. The plan for this position doesn't count on it.

4. I don't have their criteria in front of me.

5. I don't have a number for how many more tenants we'd represent, and I don't have a plan yet for after the two years. I can commit to a report to the foundation every six months on cases opened and how they ended. Starting in January I'll also ask the county clerk for court-wide outcome data, so we'll have a comparison next year. The clinic is the Tenant Defense Project. Please leave the county name out.

I kept the summary under 300 words and wrote it around what you told me.

<final_document>
**Project Summary: Tenant Defense Project, Eviction Defense Attorney**

Last year, 1,140 eviction cases were filed in our county. The Tenant Defense Project is a two-attorney legal aid clinic, and we represented the tenant in 163 of those cases, about one in seven. We turned away roughly 300 more tenants who asked for help because no attorney was free. Each of our attorneys carries about 80 open cases.

When we represent a tenant, the results are concrete. In 58% of our cases, the tenant either stayed in the home or got at least 60 days to move. That is time to find new housing and keep children in their schools.

Our capacity is about to shrink. One of our two attorneys leaves in June 2027. We ask for $90,000 over two years ($45,000 a year) toward a new staff attorney. The departing attorney will spend her last month training the new hire, so open cases and clients carry over without a gap. Whatever happens with her position, this grant keeps at least two attorneys working for tenants. If we can also replace her, it lets us grow to three.

**Budget.** The position costs $78,000 a year with benefits. A family fund has pledged $20,000 a year for both years. The clinic's general budget covers the remaining $13,000 a year. The plan does not depend on our county contract, which is up for renewal in October 2027.

**Accountability.** Every six months we will report to the Foundation on the cases we opened and how they ended. Starting in January 2027, we will ask the county clerk for court-wide eviction outcome data. That will let us compare outcomes for tenants with and without a lawyer, and we will share the comparison with the Foundation.
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **The hire is framed as keeping capacity, not adding it.** You don't know yet whether you can replace the departing attorney, so the summary doesn't claim you'll definitely have three lawyers. It says the grant guarantees at least two and makes three possible. If you get replacement funding before you submit, change that to a clear three-attorney expansion. That's a stronger case.
- **Check the timing.** For the training month to happen, the new attorney has to start by May 2027. Make sure the foundation's grant period allows that.
- **I left two things out on purpose.** There's no estimate of additional tenants served, and no plan for after the two years. If the full application asks about sustainability, reviewers will notice, so even a sentence on how you'll pursue ongoing funding would help.
